standard.title: Language carries cultural meaning
standard.description: notice that language carries cultural meaning in classroom-related greetings, introductions, instructions and routines
standard.prior_knowledge: Students have noticed that language is connected to culture (AC9LSF03) and can use modelled classroom greetings and routines (AC9LS2C01). They have not yet analysed the cultural meaning embedded in specific greetings, forms of address, or non-verbal conventions.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students notice that target language greetings, introductions, instructions and routines carry cultural meaning — including forms of address, non-verbal conventions and contextual variation — and can explain some of these connections.

nodes.label: Noticing cultural meaning in greetings and forms of address
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can notice that target language greetings and forms of address carry cultural meaning — that choices about how to greet and address someone signal relationship, respect and context.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least two instances where a greeting or form of address in the target language signals something about relationship or context.
nodes.typical_width: Explain the cultural significance of contextually varied greetings, formal and informal address distinctions, and address conventions for different relationships; create resources explaining cultural terms; compare target language and English greeting conventions.
wider: Explain a target language greeting convention to someone outside the classroom — articulate what the convention means and why it matters
Compare formal and informal address conventions in the target language with equivalent conventions in English or another language known to the class
nodes.hinge_reason: Understanding that language choices carry cultural meaning is the conceptual foundation for all cultural and intercultural work. Students who treat greetings as arbitrary phrases cannot engage with the richer cultural meaning work in node 2 or at subsequent bands.

response_modes.reason: The connection between language form and cultural meaning must be made explicit — students need to ask 'why is this form used here?' not just 'what does this mean?'. Tasks requiring explanation of cultural reasons build the analytical habit.

success_criteria: Identifies at least two target language greetings or address forms and explains what relationship or context each signals
Can distinguish at least one formal and one informal address form and explain when each is appropriate

nodes.label: Noticing non-verbal communication and cultural expressions
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can notice that body language, tone, gesture and culturally specific expressions carry meaning in target language interaction — and that these sometimes differ from English conventions.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least one non-verbal feature (gesture, body language, tone) that carries meaning in target language interaction and explain what it communicates.
nodes.typical_width: Notice body language and tone in target language expressions; compare non-verbal conventions in target language and English contexts; recognise that gesture and facial expression are integral to communication; explore culturally specific expressions and compare with English equivalents.
wider: Demonstrate a target language non-verbal convention and explain its meaning to a partner — including the equivalent or near-equivalent in English
Explore expressions in Australian English that carry cultural meaning and compare with target language equivalents — identify what each reveals about cultural priorities

response_modes.reason: Non-verbal and cultural meaning is most visible across varied examples in different communicative domains. Varied exposure builds the generalisation that cultural meaning is embedded in language use across all contexts.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Connecting non-verbal communication conventions across target language, English and First Nations communication practices positions language learning as genuinely intercultural from the earliest stages.
success_criteria: Identifies at least one non-verbal convention that carries cultural meaning in target language interaction and explains what it communicates
Compares at least one target language cultural expression with an English equivalent and describes the similarity or difference
